newsitem.title: USA: FTC commissioners to vote on Staples deal.
newsitem.headline: FTC commissioners to vote on Staples deal.

text.p: Staples Inc. and Office Depot provided last-minute information to Federal Trade Commissioners Thursday, one day before the five-member FTC votes whether to approve a modified merger agreement.

The two office superstore chains restructured a proposed $4 billion merger after the FTC turned down their first proposal last month, 4-1. At the time, the FTC voted to go to Federal District Court to fight the deal.
In their new proposal, the two chains offered to divest 63 stores to the third player in the office superstore field, OfficeMax Inc.
A representative of OfficeMax met with FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky on Thursday.
"Our representatives have been communicating with both staff and commission throughout this process including today," a spokesman for OfficeMax said. OfficeMax strongly supports the deal.

A spokesman for Staples expressed optimism that the commission would rule for the merger. If Office Depot and Staples merge the new chain would have more than 1,000 stores, competing with an OfficeMax chain of roughly 800 stores.
On Wednesday, lawyers for Staples and Office Depot met with Pitofsky. Pitofsky and others requested the additional information, which was provided to them Thursday.
The commission is to consider the modified proposal to merge in the form of a "consent decree."
In making its decision, the commission will take in the views of a split staff. In fact, the commission will consider -- as it always does -- four separate reports.
The director of the Bureau of Competition, an attorney, filed one report. His staff filed a separate report.
The director of the Bureau of Economics, an economist, filed another report. And his staff filed a separate report, too.
Representatives of those who wrote the four reports will be at the meeting to answer questions from the commission.
In addition, the commission will take into account data from Staples and Office Depot.
Pitofsky was said to have had a relatively warm meeting with representatives of Office Depot and Staples earlier this week.
